title.en: The man who lives next door

goal.sl: Poveš, katero osebo ali stvar misliš, v enem stavku (the man who lives next door, the cheese Arthur likes), s where, whose in predlogom na koncu.
goal.de: Du sagst in einem Satz, welche Person oder Sache du meinst (the man who lives next door, the cheese Arthur likes), mit where, whose und dem kleinen Wort am Ende.
goal.it: Dici in una frase quale persona o cosa intendi (the man who lives next door, the cheese Arthur likes), con where, whose e la parolina in fondo.
goal.en: You can say in one sentence which person or thing you mean (the man who lives next door, the cheese Arthur likes), with where, whose and the small word at the end.

say.sl: **who** poveže dva stavka o osebi in pove, katero osebo misliš: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (Mož, ki živi zraven, je kovač.) **That's the woman who runs the inn.** (To je ženska, ki vodi gostilno.) **who** stoji takoj za osebo, brez vejice, čeprav jo slovenščina zahteva.
say.de: **who** verbindet zwei Sätze über eine Person und sagt, welche du meinst: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (Der Mann, der nebenan wohnt, ist Schmied.) **That's the woman who runs the inn.** (Das ist die Frau, die das Gasthaus führt.) **who** steht gleich nach der Person, ohne Komma, und ändert sich nie.
say.it: **who** unisce due frasi su una persona e dice quale intendi: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** (L'uomo che abita qui accanto è un fabbro.) **That's the woman who runs the inn.** (È la donna che gestisce la locanda.) **who** viene subito dopo la persona, senza virgola.
say.en: **who** joins two sentences about a person and says which person you mean: **The man who lives next door is a blacksmith.** **That's the woman who runs the inn.** **who** comes straight after the person, with no comma.

say.sl: **which** je za stvari: **the bus which goes to Keswick** (avtobus, ki pelje v Keswick). **that** je za ljudi in stvari, v govoru najpogostejši: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down** (kombi, ki se je pokvaril). Žival vzame which ali that, znana žival tudi who: **Meg's the dog who found the lamb.**
say.de: **which** ist für Dinge: **the bus which goes to Keswick** (der Bus, der nach Keswick fährt). **that** ist für Menschen und Dinge, gesprochen am häufigsten: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down** (der Lieferwagen, der eine Panne hatte). Ein Tier nimmt which oder that, ein bekanntes auch who: **Meg's the dog who found the lamb.**
say.it: **which** è per le cose: **the bus which goes to Keswick** (l'autobus che va a Keswick). **that** è per persone e cose, a voce il più comune: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down** (il furgone che si è guastato). Un animale prende which o that, uno che conosci anche who: **Meg's the dog who found the lamb.**
say.en: **which** is for things: **the bus which goes to Keswick**. **that** is for people and things, and in talk it is the most common: **the man that lives next door**, **the van that broke down**. An animal takes which or that, one you know also who: **Meg's the dog who found the lamb.**

say.sl: Če takoj za besedo pride nov osebek, je beseda predmet in lahko odpade: **the cheese that Arthur likes** = **the cheese Arthur likes** (sir, ki ga ima Arthur rad). **the man I met yesterday** (mož, ki sem ga včeraj srečal{m:|f:a}). Če pride glagol, je osebek in ostane: **the man who lives next door**. Slovenski *ga, jo* nima para: **the book I read** (knjiga, ki sem jo prebral{m:|f:a}).
say.de: Kommt gleich danach ein neues Subjekt, ist das Wort Objekt und kann wegfallen: **the cheese that Arthur likes** = **the cheese Arthur likes** (der Käse, den Arthur mag). **the man I met yesterday** (der Mann, den ich gestern getroffen habe). Kommt ein Verb, ist es Subjekt und bleibt: **the man who lives next door**. Kein Pronomen kommt dazu: **the book I read**, nie *the book I read it*.
say.it: Se subito dopo viene un nuovo soggetto, la parola è oggetto e può cadere: **the cheese that Arthur likes** = **the cheese Arthur likes** (il formaggio che piace ad Arthur). **the man I met yesterday** (l'uomo che ho incontrato ieri). Se viene un verbo, è soggetto e resta: **the man who lives next door**. Non si aggiunge un pronome: **the book I read**, mai *the book I read it*.
say.en: When a new subject comes straight after it, the word is the object and can go: **the cheese that Arthur likes** = **the cheese Arthur likes**. **the man I met yesterday**. When a verb comes next, it is the subject and stays: **the man who lives next door**. No pronoun comes in: **the book I read**, never *the book I read it*.

say.sl: **where** je za kraje: **the inn where we had lunch** (gostilna, kjer smo kosili), **the farm where Jack lives**. **whose** stoji za his, her, their: **Jack is the man whose dog won the prize.** (Jack je mož, čigar pes je dobil nagrado.) **That's the woman whose son drives the bus.** Zveni kot who's, a who's je who is.
say.de: **where** ist für Orte: **the inn where we had lunch** (das Gasthaus, wo wir gegessen haben), **the farm where Jack lives**. **whose** steht für his, her, their: **Jack is the man whose dog won the prize.** (Jack ist der Mann, dessen Hund den Preis gewonnen hat.) **That's the woman whose son drives the bus.** Es klingt wie who's, aber who's ist who is.
say.it: **where** è per i luoghi: **the inn where we had lunch** (la locanda dove abbiamo pranzato), **the farm where Jack lives**. **whose** sta per his, her, their: **Jack is the man whose dog won the prize.** (Jack è l'uomo il cui cane ha vinto il premio.) **That's the woman whose son drives the bus.** Suona come who's, ma who's è who is.
say.en: **where** is for places: **the inn where we had lunch**, **the farm where Jack lives**. **whose** stands for his, her, their: **Jack is the man whose dog won the prize.** **That's the woman whose son drives the bus.** It sounds like who's, but who's is who is.

say.sl: Mali predlog ostane na koncu, za glagolom: **the woman I spoke to** (ženska, s katero sem govoril{m:|f:a}), **the inn we had lunch at**, **the man I work for** (mož, pri katerem delam). Slovenščina ga da naprej, angleščina ne. Zelo uradno gre naprej z **whom**: **the man for whom I work**.
say.de: Das kleine Wort bleibt am Ende, nach dem Verb: **the woman I spoke to** (die Frau, mit der ich gesprochen habe), **the inn we had lunch at**, **the man I work for** (der Mann, für den ich arbeite). Deutsch stellt es nach vorn, Englisch nicht. Nur sehr förmlich geht es nach vorn mit **whom**: **the man for whom I work**.
say.it: La parolina resta in fondo, dopo il verbo: **the woman I spoke to** (la donna con cui ho parlato), **the inn we had lunch at**, **the man I work for** (l'uomo per cui lavoro). L'italiano la mette davanti, l'inglese no. Solo in modo molto formale va davanti con **whom**: **the man for whom I work**.
say.en: A small word stays at the end, after its verb: **the woman I spoke to**, **the inn we had lunch at**, **the man I work for**. Only very formal English moves it to the front, with **whom**: **the man for whom I work**.

say.sl: V pisavi je **who** ali **that**: **the man who lives next door**, **There's a man who lives up at the mill.** Ljudje v mnogih krajih Britanije rečejo tudi *the man what lives next door*, tu na severu tudi *There's a man lives up at the mill*, brez besede. Oboje razumeš, napišeš pa prvo.
say.de: Geschrieben steht **who** oder **that**: **the man who lives next door**, **There's a man who lives up at the mill.** Die Leute sagen in vielen Gegenden Großbritanniens auch *the man what lives next door*, hier im Norden auch *There's a man lives up at the mill*, ganz ohne Wort. Beides verstehst du, schreiben tust du das erste.
say.it: Per iscritto si usa **who** o **that**: **the man who lives next door**, **There's a man who lives up at the mill.** In molte parti della Gran Bretagna si dice anche *the man what lives next door*, qui al nord anche *There's a man lives up at the mill*, senza parola. Capisci tutti e due, scrivi il primo.
say.en: Writing wants **who** or **that**: **the man who lives next door**, **There's a man who lives up at the mill.** In many parts of Britain people also say *the man what lives next door*, and here in the North *There's a man lives up at the mill*, with no word at all.
